source_meta._title: Projectiles don't collide with the world border

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 14w17a in a singleplayer Creative-mode Superflat world with commands/cheats enabled. Use the normal first-person view. The instructions name the default controls: T for chat, E for inventory, number keys 1–9 for hotbar selection, and right-click for Use Item; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot listed as the recommended version: Minecraft 14w17a. Do not use fix version 24w33a.
Use a new disposable world so changing the world-border center and size does not affect an existing save.
Use Creative mode and enable commands/cheats so the supplied /worldborder commands can be executed and a Snowball can be obtained without random exploration.
Use a Superflat world as a deterministic execution choice; the report does not specify a seed, coordinates, or terrain, and a flat world provides a clear projectile path.
Keep at least one empty hotbar slot available for the Snowball.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the Minecraft 14w17a installation/profile and wait for the main menu to load.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version label on the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 14w17a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Click the Game Mode button until it displays Game Mode: Creative.
steps.success_cue: Creative is displayed as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Select More World Options... to open the additional world-generation settings.
steps.success_cue: The screen containing World Type and Allow Cheats is visible.

steps.action: Click World Type until it displays World Type: Superflat.
steps.success_cue: Superflat is displayed as the selected world type.

steps.action: Set Allow Cheats to ON. If it is already ON because Creative mode was selected, leave it unchanged.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Return from More World Options if necessary, select Create New World, and wait for world generation to finish. Do not move away from the initial location after control is granted.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the Superflat surface, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement and camera controls respond normally.

steps.action: Press the Chat control, default T, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: A chat input line is visible and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's world-border center command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Both tildes refer to the player's current horizontal position: the first is X and the second is Z.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, and chat reports that the world-border center was changed.

steps.action: Without moving from the newly established center, press the Chat control, default T, again.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open again.

steps.action: Enter the report's world-border size command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The value 20 sets the square border to twenty blocks wide.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without an error, chat reports that the world-border width was set to 20 blocks, and the nearby world-border walls become visible around the player.

steps.action: Wait until the border has finished resizing, surrounding terrain remains rendered, and movement and camera controls respond normally. Because the player remained at the center of a 20-block-wide border, each nearest side should be approximately 10 blocks away.
steps.success_cue: A stable square world border surrounds the player, with the player still safely inside it near the center.

steps.action: Press the Inventory control, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and the hotbar slots are visible along its bottom edge.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon, select its search field, and search for Snowball. With an English interface, enter the text shown in exact_input.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball item appears among the filtered Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Move a stack of Snowballs from the search result into an empty hotbar slot. One reliable method is to left-click the Snowball result to pick up a stack, then left-click an empty slot in the hotbar row at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball stack is visible in a numbered hotbar slot.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory by pressing E or Escape.
steps.success_cue: First-person world view is restored and the hotbar containing the Snowball stack is visible.

steps.action: Select the Snowball's hotbar slot by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling to it.
steps.success_cue: The Snowball slot has the active-slot highlight and a Snowball is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Rotate the camera while remaining inside the border until one of the four nearby world-border walls is directly ahead. Do not move through the wall or outside the border.
steps.success_cue: A world-border wall is centered in the player's forward view approximately 10 blocks away.

steps.action: Adjust the crosshair so it points toward the world-border wall through unobstructed air at approximately eye level. Do not aim downward at the Superflat ground and do not place any block between the player and the border.
steps.success_cue: The straight path from the player's hand to the targeted part of the world border is clear of blocks and entities.

steps.action: Use the selected Snowball once by pressing the Use Item control, default right-click, while maintaining the aim established in the previous step.
steps.success_cue: One Snowball has been launched directly toward the world-border wall on an unobstructed path.

stor.handoff_condition: The Snowball has just been launched directly toward the nearby world-border wall from inside the border. Hand control immediately to the observation subsystem before changing aim, moving the player, throwing another projectile, or otherwise altering the scene.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, terrain type, game mode, or singleplayer versus multiplayer. A new singleplayer Creative Superflat world is selected only as the simplest deterministic environment that supports the supplied commands and provides a clear projectile path.

The Creative inventory's displayed item names depend on the selected language. The exact search input "snowball" assumes an English interface; in another language, use the localized name or visually locate the Snowball item.

External verification confirms that /worldborder was introduced in Java Edition 14w17a and supports the supplied center and set command forms; therefore the report's commands are preserved without modernization. ([pt.minecraft.wiki](https://pt.minecraft.wiki/w/Barreira_do_mundo?utm_source=openai))

The report states that all types of projectiles are affected but proposes a Snowball as its example. This plan tests one Snowball once, which is the minimum safe trigger supported by the report; it does not add repeated throws or alternate projectiles.
